main_text.p: 1. Hamza (ء) est servus Elif mobilis, cui cum vocali appositum, motum ejus actualem significat, ut أن، أن، أن an, on, in, & sine vocali motum ejus indicat potentialem, sil. quod | sit radicale, & naturâ suâ mobile, ut [?]لمين jamen. Sæpè tamen omittitur ut superfluum, quia motus | ex vocali adjecta facilè percipitur, sicut & posita Hamza, illud | sæpè omittitur, ita ut pro eodem usurpatur, & in pronuntiatione idem valet : idque
1, In sine, cum Hamza habet ante se unam ex literis [illegible, ~3 letters] ut [?]مـاون maon, pro [?]سـاون, [?]سـاون pro [?]سـاون, [?]سـيون shaion, pro [?]سيون.

2, In medio post literam vocali carentem, ut [?]سـول pro [?]سـول, vel post aliud | ut [?]اَندرا aandera pro [?]اَندر ; cum tamen duplex occurrit | quarum prius movetur, in quibusdam libris utrumque | exprimitur, ut [?]الدر.

page.notes: The Arabic and Hebrew-style forms are copied as best the scan allows; the vowel points and several letters in the Arabic words are doubtful and marked [?]. The Latin text is clear. Long s has been written as plain s throughout.
